title: Microsoft Purview: improved built-in sensitive information types
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap targets and distinguishes the planned improvement from existing sensitive information type capabilities. The documented controls and licensing background are supported; searches found no improvement-specific rollout setting, default or charge.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The tenant SIT inventory is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal at Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, navigate to Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types and choose Create sensitive info type.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Get-DlpSensitiveInformationType -Identity "Credit Card Number" | Format-List inspects a tenant SIT, including its recommended confidence.
claims.quote:
Get-DlpSensitiveInformationType -Identity "Credit Card Number" | Format-List
The RecommendedConfidence property of the returned objects contains a value that represents the default (or recommended) confidence level that should be used with the corresponding sensitive information type.

claims.claim: Get-DlpSensitiveInformationType is a read-only inspection cmdlet available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
Use the Get-DlpSensitiveInformationType cmdlet to list the sensitive information types that are defined for your organization

claims.claim: The Sensitive info types portal page shows match counts.
claims.quote: You can view the number of matches a SIT has in Sensitive info types and Content explorer.

claims.claim: The portal offers a Test option for selected SITs.
claims.quote: You can test the SIT by uploading a sample file. The test results show the number of matches for each confidence level. You can test built-in SITs, custom SITs, trainable classifiers, and exact data match.

claims.claim: A built-in SIT can be copied in the Microsoft Purview portal at Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types > sensitive information type > Copy.
claims.quote:
Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types and select the sensitive information type that you want to copy.
The overview page for the sensitive information type opens. Choose Copy.

claims.claim: New-DlpSensitiveInformationTypeRulePackage -FileData ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('PathToUnicodeXMLFile')) uploads XML defining a custom SIT rather than editing a built-in SIT.
claims.quote:
To upload your rule package, do the following steps:
1. Save it as an .xml file with Unicode encoding.
2. Connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell
3. Use the following syntax:
New-DlpSensitiveInformationTypeRulePackage -FileData ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('PathToUnicodeXMLFile'))

claims.claim: Some SITs cannot be copied, and the custom SIT creation page lists them.
claims.quote:
These SITs can't be copied:
- Canada driver's license number
- EU driver's license number
- EU national identification number
- EU passport number
